headline: Oil-and-politics shock knocks the KSE-100 down 1.41% — even OGDC and Mari got sold, so the desk is leaning cautious and picky, not defensive across the board.
summary: The KSE-100 fell 1.41% to 177,955.51 today as the US-Iran ceasefire deadline lapsed, oil neared three-week highs, and a Supreme Court order moving Imran Khan to hospital added political noise. Even OGDC and Mari — usually oil-price winners — got sold with everything else, a sign this was broad risk-off, not sector logic. Inflation is cooling (CPI 9.2% in July) and rates held at 11.5%, but a firmer dollar and softer rupee argue for caution on cyclicals. With the geo-risk gauge at a 'moderate' 59/100, the desk's read is patience and quality over chasing the dip — bank carry books and select oversold names, not broad exposure.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Broadly capped by the risk-off regime (UBL was today's single biggest drag), but banks with strong T-bill/PIB books still earn a carry cushion with 6M T-bills at 11.70% and 10Y PIBs at 12.30% against an 11.5% policy rate.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas Exploration (E&P)
sectors.why: Structural beneficiary of the Hormuz-driven oil-supply-risk premium (Brent near 3-week highs), though OGDC and Mari were sold off with the broader tape today — the thesis argues patience over chasing it.

sectors.name: Refineries / OMCs
sectors.why: Hormuz-adjacent shipping disruption and elevated crude are a physical supply-security and margin risk for names like ATRL, not just a price story.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Import- and energy-cost-intensive and named among today's broad sell-off sectors as oil pushes higher.

sectors.name: Automobile Assemblers
sectors.why: Same import- and energy-cost exposure as cement, and most exposed to a sustained oil-price/PKR shock.

sectors.name: Textiles / Exporters
sectors.why: FY26 current account already closed in a marginal deficit on import pressure; a sustained oil shock compounds that before fresher data confirms the FY27 trend.

watchlist.angle: The desk's highest-confidence live signal today: an OBV volume-leads-price divergence with a 96.6% historical hit rate and +5.11% net expectancy over 89 trades (83.3% out-of-sample hit rate). Fundamentals back it up — 'attractive' rating, P/E of 6.52 (cheap third of PSX) and a strong 32.2% net margin. Freshly reinforced by news: a Rs10bn sponsor capital injection was approved today.
watchlist.risk: No dividend, so the return depends entirely on price — and it's still a Commercial Bank name in a sector the risk-off regime otherwise caps.

watchlist.angle: A live trend + momentum combo trigger (56.8% hit rate, +1.25% net expectancy, medium confidence) and cheap fundamentals (P/E 5.51, 13% net margin, 'mixed' rating) — but flagged with a caveat, not a lead pick.
watchlist.risk: Automobile Assemblers are explicitly on the desk's risk-off avoid list today (import- and energy-cost exposure), and the fundamental rating is only 'mixed,' not a clean stack — this one is logged for watching, not chasing.

watchlist.angle: No active technical trigger today, but it's the clean version of the desk's one risk-off carve-out — a bank with a strong fixed-income book, an 'attractive' fundamental rating (cheap P/E, healthy margin, covered dividend), and a confirmed book-closure/dividend catalyst on 2026-08-20 (Rs1.5, 1.52% yield).
watchlist.risk: Banks broadly are capped in this regime — the case here rests specifically on the carry/dividend angle, not a momentum or breakout signal.

catalysts.event: SBP MTB auction (~Rs500bn target) inside the new Rs5.4trn Aug-Oct borrowing plan
FABL book closure, Rs1.5 dividend (1.52% yield)
SBP weekly FX reserves print — watched for whether the 3-week gain streak extends
BWCL and HMB book closures, Rs10.0 and Rs2.5 dividends respectively
MSCI Frontier Market Small Cap reconstitution effective (AIRLINK added, Biafo Industries removed)
SBP MPC — next rate decision, now shadowed by oil-price risk to the further-cuts outlook

risks: The US-Iran ceasefire deadline expired without a deal — a further Hormuz shipping disruption would push oil and the PKR/import bill higher and could deepen the sell-off rather than let it fade.

The Supreme Court's Imran Khan hospital-transfer order keeps a domestic political overhang live ahead of the next hearing on 2026-09-16, adding a second source of headline risk on top of the external shock.

Today's -1.41% close was broad risk-off, not sector-specific — even the geo-risk gauge's 'moderate' (not extreme) 59/100 band leaves room for further foreign-outflow-driven selling if VIX and gold keep climbing.
